findings.claim: Log injection vulnerability: implementation uses req.path (percent-decoded) instead of raw URL path; spec requires path logged 'without percent-decoding', allowing newlines and spaces in %0A/%20 to break format and inject fake log lines

findings.claim: Test for AC-3 (empty q value) cannot fail if the `if (q)` conditional check is removed from the implementation.
findings.evidence: Line 78 asserts `assert.deepEqual(await res.json(), items)` after querying with `?q=`. If the filter ran unconditionally with `needle = ''`, every item would still match because `'any string'.includes('')` is always `true` in JavaScript. The test cannot distinguish between 'correctly skips filter' and 'filter runs but matches everything'.

findings.claim: Test for AC-4 (bare q key with no value) has the same tautology as AC-3 and cannot fail.
findings.evidence: Line 88 asserts `assert.deepEqual(await res.json(), items)` after querying with bare `?q`. Express parses this as empty string, and the same `String.prototype.includes('')` always-true condition applies. Removing the `if (q)` check would not cause the test to fail.

Verify no out-of-scope changes: confirmed route response contracts unchanged, only stdout used, no new dependencies, no flags beyond NODE_ENV, no modification to test helpers/existing tests/server.js
Verify timing implementation: process.hrtime.bigint() for nanosecond precision properly converted to milliseconds with Math.round()
Verify path handling: req.originalUrl.split('?')[0] correctly preserves raw path without decoding and excludes query string
Verify NODE_ENV re-evaluation per-request: check is inside res.on('finish') callback, not cached at module/createApp time, allowing runtime toggling
Attempt to inject newlines in URL path via percent-encoding (%0A) to break one-line-per-request invariant — blocked by preserving raw originalUrl without decoding
Attempt to leak secrets in query strings (e.g., GET /items?api_key=secret) — blocked by splitting on '?' to exclude query strings
Attempt to bypass NODE_ENV suppression by modifying process.env at runtime — evaluated per-request per spec requirement (ac-9), general platform concern not implementation defect
Attempt to trigger logging of Authorization headers or session tokens — blocked by middleware accessing only method, path, status code, elapsed time; no header access
Attempt to cause logging of POST request bodies or sensitive payload data — blocked by implementation never accessing req.body or response contents

Type validation: Repeated keys (?q=a&q=b) and bracketed keys (?q[x]=y) must be rejected as 400 with 'invalid q' error. The implementation correctly checks typeof q !== 'string' after confirming q is not undefined, catching both array and object types that Express parses from these malformed inputs.

Filtering logic: Case-insensitive substring matching must run on the full insertion-ordered list before limit cap. For ?q=widget&limit=2 on [widget, other, widget, widget], should return 2 widgets not 'first 2 items filtered'. Implementation correctly places filter stage before sort and cap stages, and applies toLowerCase() to both needle and haystack.

Pipeline order: Verify filter→sort→cap sequencing AC-11 and AC-13 integration. The implementation processes validation (q, sort, limit), then filter on full list, then sort, then cap—exactly as specified. Limit validation runs independently regardless of q validity.

attempts: Attempted to break path extraction by sending query strings and percent-encoded paths (ac-5): implementation correctly strips query string while preserving encoding, test passes

Attempted to break timing measurement by checking for correct millisecond format without decimal points or units (ac-6): implementation uses process.hrtime.bigint() and Math.round() producing integers, test validates format and range

Attempted to break NODE_ENV caching by changing process.env at runtime between requests (ac-9): implementation re-evaluates NODE_ENV inside res.on('finish') per request, test confirms dynamic evaluation across three requests

Verified all 14 acceptance criteria: q validation, case-insensitive matching, empty-string handling, non-matching 200-array, order preservation, error handling for non-string q, filter-before-cap ordering, and isolation of GET /items from other routes—all implemented correctly per spec language.

Confirmed the diff stays within spec.touched_surfaces (toy/src/app.js and API definition) and violates none of the out_of_scope constraints: no limit/sort implementation, no Item shape changes, no POST /items changes, no server/package/helpers modifications, and no other route changes.

Deep-dive on filter implementation: verified literal-substring matching via String.includes() (not regex), no trimming, URL-decoded verbatim, contiguous-only matching, read-only (no mutations to items map), and pipeline order (filter→sort→cap) correctly applies the q filter to the full insertion-ordered list before the limit cap.
Attempted string injection via `.includes()` using payload `%27%29.filter%28` — blocked because `.includes()` is a safe string method that treats input as literal characters, not code

Attempted prototype pollution via repeated parameters `?q=a&q=b` and bracket notation `?q[x]=y` — blocked by line 25 type check `if (q !== undefined && typeof q !== 'string')` which rejects arrays and objects before filter logic executes

Attempted ReDoS via regex metacharacters `.*+?^$|()[]{}` — blocked because implementation uses `.includes()` (linear substring search) not regex, eliminating backtracking and exponential time behavior
Attempted authorization bypass by manipulating `q` to escalate privileges — blocked by spec scope (auth is out of scope) and implementation (parameter only filters results, adds no auth logic)
Attempted information disclosure in error responses — blocked by generic error message `{ error: 'invalid q' }` with no details about invalid value, matching project convention

Test that empty q parameter returns all items unchanged (AC-3, AC-4): filtering is skipped by the falsy check `if (q)`, allowing default behavior to match spec requirement that 'an empty q returns everything, exactly as today'

Test that repeated q parameter or bracketed q object both reject with 400 invalid q (AC-9): the code validates `typeof q !== 'string'` to reject Express's array/object parsing, matching the 'invalid q' error convention

Test that q filter is applied to the full list before limit cap is applied (AC-11): the filter stage processes all items before the cap stage calls slice(0, limit), ensuring 'the cap never counts an item that q excluded'

Test that case-insensitive substring matching works in both directions (AC-2): the implementation converts both q and item.name to lowercase with toLowerCase() before calling includes(), covering 'matching is plain, literal String.prototype.includes on both sides lower-cased'

Test that q parameter is ignored on routes other than GET /items collection (AC-14): q validation and filtering logic only exist within the `app.get('/items', ...)` handler, leaving GET /items/:id, GET /health, and POST /items unaffected
Test that matching is literal with no trimming, regex, or accent folding (AC-10): the code uses plain includes() without calling trim() or applying any transformations beyond toLowerCase()
